conviction_note: Nothing company-level and unpriced was found for the reported quarter. FSP is a $0.45, roughly $47m-equity office REIT carrying $266m+ of 9% TPG debt. The Q3 print is mostly noise (no call, no guidance, dividend suspended, FFO about $0.01-0.02), so the move turns on whether the release carries a strategic-review update; no 8-K since July says no deal has been signed. abs_move is set above the 4.51% historical median for 84% realised vol, a 25% 20-day run-up and the two-sided strategic tail. p_up is 46 rather than 50 because 5 of the last 7 prints fell and the run-up was bought by one 13D holder, with nothing new likely in the release. The findings sum (-1.0) and the scaled number (-0.52) agree in sign and both are small.
bar: unsourced: no consensus EPS/FFO found from two agreeing sources and the company gives no guidance. The implicit bar is the Q2 2026 run-rate: revenue $26.36m, FFO $0.02/share, AFFO $0.01, 67.4% leased (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001031316/000110465926087553/fsp-20260728xex99d2.htm). Q3 revenue should dip slightly because Greenwood Plaza was sold 2026-07-08. Every finding is capped small.

Not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. There is no option chain (empty_chain), so no skew. findings.finding: Powell Anderson Capital / R. Adam Lindsay filed a Schedule 13D on 2026-10-14 showing 6.8% (7.07m shares), bought from 2026-08-17 to 2026-10-14 at $0.31-0.48 for about $2.9m. Item 4 states no present plan or proposal: a passive-value purchase, not an activist demand. The stock has since run +25% over 20 days to $0.45, so part of the run-up is one buyer's accumulation and not anticipation of news in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior 13D-driven run into a print in the baseline. The last 7 prints moved 0.0, -4.55, -8.33, -4.51, -1.16, +1.94 and +6.01 (5 of 7 down), with Q2 2026 flat.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is already in the price. The open question is whether a release with no deal gives some of it back. If the market had priced the buying as merely passive, the stock would not have re-rated 25% into an earnings release that carries no call and no guidance.
findings.independence: Run-up figures come from the sealed baseline (run_up_20d_pct 25.0, run_up_5d_pct 15.38), a separate source from the filing. Nothing else independent.

findings.finding: Occupancy is drifting down: 68.9% leased at 2025-12-31, 68.4% at Q1 and 67.4% at Q2 2026, because expirations exceeded new leases. Only about 3.0% of square footage expires in 2026 against 11.5% in 2027, so the Q3 decline is likely small. The JLL marketing book for 11 of the assets shows 61% occupancy and $36m in-place NOI.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Occupancy declines have printed without large moves: Q2 2026, with a 1-point leased decline, closed 0.0%; Q1 2026 -4.55%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the trend is public. Only the Q3 increment is new. A sharp leased drop would show up as a larger reaction than the history's median. The low 2026 expiry schedule argues for a small increment.
findings.independence: JLL listing (61% occupancy on the marketed assets): https://invest.jll.com/us/en/listings/office/franklin-street-properties-portfolio

findings.finding: Greenwood Plaza (Englewood, CO) was sold 2026-07-08 for a gross $19.4m at about a $7.7m loss, which was already impaired in Q2. About $8.5m of proceeds repaid the TPG term loan and about $8.9m of cash was retained. Q3 loses that asset's rent and records the sale; no new loss should be expected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print, which carried the $7.7m impairment, closed 0.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: disclosed in July with an 8-K (2026-07-13). Only the small revenue run-rate hit lands in Q3.

findings.finding: The expanded strategic review (BofA Securities plus JLL as co-advisors since April 2026, covering corporate, portfolio and single-asset sales) has been marketing 11 assets, 4.61m sf, at 61% occupancy and $36m in-place NOI, whole or by market, since at least June 2026. No transaction 8-K has been filed since 2026-07-28, so no definitive deal is signed. The Q3 release will likely carry a status line, and against a roughly $47m equity stub under $266m+ of debt, any price signal moves the stock hard in either direction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose when the strategic review was announced in May 2025 (per search snippet). Later review updates came with the -8.33% (2026-03-09, dividend suspension and refinancing) and -4.55% (2026-04-28) prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is unknowable from public documents; it is priced as an option-like stub. If the market expected a deal, the run-up would sit alongside an 8-K or press leak, and none exists. The finding is sized 0 with a wide band, and that width goes into abs_move_pct.
findings.independence: Q2 release language on the expanded review: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001031316/000110465926087553/fsp-20260728xex99d1.htm

findings.finding: The TPG term loans (refinanced 2026-03-04, $320m facility) carry 9.0% interest (13.0% if extended), a 6% OID, a 4% exit fee, make-whole inside year one, and mandatory prepayment from disposition proceeds. Asset-sale proceeds therefore go to the lender before the equity. Covenants are minimum tangible net worth and $5m minimum liquidity; the company was compliant at 2026-06-30 with $22.5m of cash, down from $30.6m at year-end, and the 10-Q has no going-concern language. What the money bought was the retirement of the old term loans and senior notes, i.e. a maturity extension to 2029, not growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The refinancing quarter (2026-03-09 print, with the dividend suspension) closed -8.33%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; the terms are public. A Q3 cash burn that brings liquidity nearer the covenant floor would be new. Six-month operating cash use was only $2.1m, so that risk is small this quarter.
findings.independence: Same 10-Q as the occupancy finding; the 8-K of 2026-03-04 (Items 1.01/2.03) is the primary for the facility.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The mild negative lean cuts against the +25% run-up, but that run-up has an identified cause (13D accumulation), so the lean is mostly a fade of an un-catalysed run into an information-light print, and p_up stays close to 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the term loan refinanced debt and extended maturity to 2029; covenants are compliant and there is no going-concern language, so -0.3 went to -0.1.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the Greenwood loss was already impaired in Q2 and has no path to guidance, so -0.2 went to -0.1.
Lesson 5/7 (positioning is not a cause unless explained): the 13D explains the run-up, so the fade is weaker evidence; -0.5 went to -0.3.
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism': every sign was negative, so p_up moved from 45 to 46 and abs_move stayed at 6.5.
The occupancy and strategic-review findings were left standing.
